subject: Post-call: idempotency & retry patterns for bulk inference
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.inference>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 19:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: idempotency & retry patterns for bulk inference

Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our side so we can move the POC forward. Short TL;DR at the top, then technical asks.

TL;DR: Acme's bulk inference workload (batch image captions + reranker pass) will benefit from request-level idempotency and a retry/backoff policy that distinguishes between transient 429s and overloaded GPU failures. We recommend: (1) client-generated idempotency keys for all batch requests, (2) exponential backoff with jitter for 429/503, (3) a token-based quota fence for predictable throughput during ramp.

Key notes from the call:
- Workload: nightly and on-demand bulk runs, peak concurrency ~120 parallel requests, average batch size ~300 items.
- Critical SLOs: 95th p99 latency target for on-demand reranks < 600ms per item; nightly can be lower throughput.
- Auth: Acme will use OAuth2 service account tokens; they prefer short-lived tokens with automatic refresh in the SDK.
- Routing: want requests to prefer us-east region but failover to us-west during capacity issues.
- Structured output/tool calling: POC will include a reranker that returns structured JSON tuples and a tool-calling step that invokes internal enrichment.

Technical asks (what we need from Acme):
1) Example request flow (payload size / shape) for a single batch and an expected success rate target.
2) A short-lived service account key (or guidance on the KMS you use) so we can validate OAuth flow in the SDK sandbox.
3) A sample of your retry behaviour today (do you dedupe with request id? how do you handle partial successes?).

Proposed Redwood action items (I assigned internal owners in the attached MAP):
- Create idempotency SDK helper in node/python for client-generated request IDs and idempotency headers (Owner: @lauren_bishop).
- Draft a recommended retry strategy doc for 429/503 errors with backoff parameters tuned to your concurrency (Owner: @markus_klein).
- Build a small demo showing routing preference + graceful fallback to us-west (Owner: @sergio_alvarez).

Attachments: acme-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (mutual action plan with milestones) and idempotency-retry-patterns.pdf (first-draft guidance).

Next steps: can you confirm the sample payloads and share a point of contact on DevOps for token provisioning? If we can get that by EOD Thu, we’ll have a draft SDK helper and retry doc by Fri.

Best,
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Rivera <alex@acme-cloud.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.inference>
Cc: DevOps Team <devops@acme-cloud.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: idempotency & retry patterns for bulk inference

Thanks Sergio — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Payloads: each batch request is a JSON array of items; average per-item tokenized size ~120 tokens, typical batch payload ~120KB, worst-case 800KB.
2) Auth: We can create a short-lived service account for the POC, but we'd like to validate how Redwood's SDK handles token rotation. DevOps will create the account and share a single scoped credential with you.
3) Quota model: we currently throttle per-project to avoid noisy neighbors; that's a soft quota enforced by us. We'd prefer Redwood to expose a token-quota header so we can visualize consumption.

Questions: 
- For idempotency, do you expect idempotency keys to be client-provided UUIDs or do you offer server-side generated request IDs we should echo?
- How do you recommend handling partial successes (e.g., 250/300 succeeded)? Will Redwood return a per-item status in the structured response?

We can share a sample payload and a small dataset by EOD. DevOps (cc'd) — can you confirm who will own the service account?

Alex
VP Product, Acme Cloud

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.inference>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.inference>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.inference>, Alex Rivera <alex@acme-cloud.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: idempotency & retry patterns for bulk inference

Looping in a quick internal note so Alex sees our proposed defaults before we finalize the doc.

Proposed default behavior (short):
- Idempotency: require client-generated idempotency-key header (x-redwood-idempotency-key). SDK helpers will generate a v4 UUID per batch by default and expose a hook to override. Keys expire server-side after 24 hours.
- Retries: for 429 and 502/503 return codes, use exponential backoff with full jitter: base=200ms, cap=10s, max_attempts=6. For 413 (payload too large) do not retry — return a helpful error.
- Partial success: server will return a top-level status and per-item statuses in the structured JSON with item-level error codes. Our SDK will provide a helper that can automatically retry only failed item sub-batches when safe (idempotency keys still apply).
- Quotas: support a response header X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining and a client-side quota fence in SDK (token-bucket) to limit burst behaviour; we can instrument Prometheus metrics for your dashboard.

Markus, can you draft the short example payloads for the doc and the jitter/backoff chart? I'll start the SDK helper PR after we have the sample payload.

—Lauren
Senior SWE, SDKs

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@acme-cloud.com>, DevOps Team <devops@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.inference>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: idempotency & retry patterns for bulk inference

Alex / DevOps — great, thanks for confirming. Two quick decisions so we can proceed: 

1) Idempotency: we'll expect client-generated UUIDs in x-redwood-idempotency-key. SDKs will default to generating them. For backward compatibility we’ll accept X-Request-Id but recommend using the idempotency header for batch dedupe semantics.
2) Partial success: Redwood will return JSON with a top-level "overall_status" and an "items" array where each entry has "status":"ok|error" and an optional "error_code". The SDK helper will expose a convenience method to re-submit only error items in a new batch while preserving the original idempotency context.

Action items and timelines: 
- DevOps to create scoped service account + share a single test credential (Alex/DevOps) — target: Thu EOD.
- Redwood: initial SDK helper + retry doc + demo routing (Sergio/Lauren/Markus) — target: Fri COB.
- Next call: Tue Mar 23, 10am PT to review the POC run results.

If you prefer, I can open a draft in the shared Drive and drop in the examples from Markus.

Thanks — looking forward to the POC.

Sergio
